topic: Diffusion Models for 3D Shape and Scene Generation: Methods, Representations, and Evaluation

per_sentence.text: Li et al. per_sentence.text: Prior approaches have explored a variety of representations: ShapeGF learns distributions over gradient fields that model shape surfaces, while IM-GAN represents shapes as neural fields and l-GAN trains GANs over latent variables that encode shapes; in contrast, r-GAN generates point clouds directly, and PDGN introduces progressive deconvolutional networks within a point cloud GAN framework, with SP-GAN further employing a spherical representation (Li et al., 2026).

judge.rationale: The cited paper describes a dual diffusion model for 3D avatar generation from text/image prompts and does not mention ShapeGF, IM-GAN, l-GAN, r-GAN, PDGN, SP-GAN, or any of the specific representation methods claimed in the sentence.

per_sentence.text: Building on diffusion-based principles, Li et al. (2026) describe a multi-view depth generation process that initializes from 2D maps of pure Gaussian noise and proceeds via ancestral sampling.

per_sentence.text: The inference process itself introduces practical hurdles; for instance, the multi-view depth diffusion approach described by Li et al. per_sentence.text: Furthermore, the diversity of underlying representations—ranging from gradient fields (ShapeGF) and neural fields (IM-GAN) to latent-variable GANs and point cloud generators (r-GAN, PDGN, SP-GAN)—underscores a broader challenge: no single representation has emerged as universally optimal for balancing quality, efficiency, and controllability across different 3D generation tasks (Li et al., 2026).
